records.text: Owens said that during French elections dating to 1999, it emerged that the French government had trafficked military-grade weapons to Angola through a network involving France, Russia, Slovakia, and Brenco International.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyways, it gets discovered during the course of French elections, and this is dating back to 1999, that the French government is actually involved in trafficking weapons, military-grade weapons to Angola to facilitate this war. and they did this through an illicit network of countries. The public learns this and it turns out that France is involved, Russia is involved, Slovakia is involved. They're using this company, which is known as Brenco International, to sell these arms to the Angolan president.

verification.notes: Reliable histories confirm that Falcone and Gaydamak brokered large arms shipments from Eastern Europe, including through Slovak supplier ZTS-OSOS and Falcone's Brenco network, to Angola during the 1990s. But Global Witness dates the public emergence of Angolagate to the end of 2000, not French elections in 1999, and the record describes private brokers operating from France rather than a demonstrated French-government program trafficking the weapons. The network description is substantially supported; the discovery timing and characterization of the French government overstate the evidence.
